Hi all — following up with the lab readout and some concrete numbers from the config we discussed. TL;DR: baseline meets your p99 target with the candidate model + int8 profile on our sim workload, but latency increases sharply at bursty 2k+ concurrent streams without prefilling KV cache. See details below.

Summary (lab sim, 512-token avg):
- Config: 2 x A100-like, batch cap 128, continuous batching enabled, async IO.
- p50: 42ms; p95: 118ms; p99: 198ms.
- Token cost estimate: ~$0.0038/token at observed throughput with shared cache enabled.
- Observed caveat: cold-start p99 (empty KV cache) spikes to ~600ms for first few requests; prefix caching reduces that within 5 requests.

Recommendations:
- If user experience is sensitive to cold starts, enable pre-warming and KV cache persistence between bursts.
- For peak burst tolerance, add a small buffer of scaled-up nodes to absorb 2-3x traffic surges.

Attached: p99_latency_summary.csv (detailed percentile breakdown by request size) and throughput_sim_config.yaml (the exact sim config and commands). If you want, we can run the sim against a redacted slice of your production logs (needs s3 or dropbox link).

Happy to jump on a quick 15-min call to walk the numbers — Jordan, if they share availability I can run a short live demo of the KV warm-up effect.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
